title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. pi_{0,3} denotes the profinite fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,infinity}, a free profinite group of rank 2. It sits with index 6 in an extended group pi~_{0,3}. That group is generated by sigma_inf (of order 2) and rho (of order 3), so it is essentially the profinite completion of PSL_2(Z) = Z/2 * Z/3, with pi_{0,3} corresponding to the free normal subgroup of index 6 with quotient S_3. Lower-case sigma_inf(x), rho(x) denote conjugation by these elements. The element eps_0 = sigma_inf rho is a 'half-loop' with eps_0^2 = l_0, the loop around 0. Similarly eps_1 = rho(eps_0), eps_inf = rho^2(eps_0), with squares l_1, l_inf.

The automorphism u. u is an automorphism of pi~_{0,3}, normalised by u(sigma_inf) = h sigma_inf and u(rho) = g rho with g, h in pi_{0,3}. Equations (2) of the previous section express that these images still have orders 2 and 3: h sigma_inf(h) = 1 and g rho(g) rho^2(g) = 1. The 'loop relation' (5) of the previous page is u(eps_0) = int(f^{-1}) eps_0^mu, with mu in Zhat^*. The previous page also records Grothendieck's sign conventions (f_0 replaced by f_0^{-1}, h_0 = g_0 sigma_inf(g_0)^{-1}), chosen to make the rho / sigma_inf symmetry visible.

Step 1, equations (7)-(8). Conjugating (5) by u(rho) = g rho gives the analogous relations at 1 and at infinity, with f_1 = rho(f) g^{-1} and f_inf = rho(f_1) g^{-1} = rho^2(f) rho(g)^{-1} g^{-1}. I checked this: u(rho(x)) = int(g rho) u(x), hence f_1^{-1} = g rho(f)^{-1}.

Step 2, equation (9). Write f for f_0 and rewrite (5) as int(f) u(eps_0) = eps_0^mu. Expanding:
- int(f) u(eps_0) = f h sigma_inf g rho f^{-1}
- = f h sigma_inf(g) eps_0 f^{-1}
- = [f h sigma_inf(g rho(f)^{-1})] eps_0,
 using eps_0(f) = sigma_inf(rho(f)). The bracket lies in pi_{0,3}.

Step 3. Hence f h sigma_inf(g rho(f)^{-1}) = eps_0^{mu-1}. Since mu is a unit of Zhat, its 2-adic component is odd, so mu - 1 = 2 nu with nu in Zhat. Then eps_0^{mu-1} = l_0^nu lies in pi_{0,3}, consistently. Applying sigma_inf (which sends l_0 to l_1 in his conventions) gives sigma_inf(f) sigma_inf(h) g rho(f)^{-1} = l_1^nu.

Step 4, on the next page. This leads to the boxed 'relation des lacets' (11): sigma_inf(h) g = sigma_inf(f)^{-1} l_1^nu rho(f). It links the order-2 datum h and the order-3 datum g through (f, nu). The next page adds:
- the effect of inner automorphisms on (f, g, h);
- the parametrisations g = alpha rho(alpha)^{-1} and h = beta sigma_inf(beta)^{-1}, i.e. torsion elements in a free product are conjugate into a factor.

This is the derivation of Drinfeld-Ihara type GT relations (the 2-cycle and 3-cycle relations) from automorphisms of the profinite (2,3,infinity) triangle group that respect inertia.
errors: In (9) the second form of the bracket is written as if it began with f_1 ('[f_1 h sigma_inf(g rho(f)^{-1})]'). The line just above shows the factor must be f = f_0 (as the next line, listing the factors f, h, sigma_inf(g rho(f))^{-1}, confirms). This is a slip or ambiguous handwriting, not a mathematical error.
The listing 'sigma_inf(g rho(f))^{-1}' has the inverse misplaced relative to sigma_inf(g rho(f)^{-1}); this is a notational slip.
No substantive errors otherwise. The parity claim mu - 1 in 2 Zhat is correct because units of Zhat are odd at 2.

ideas.what: Encoding GT-type data as automorphisms u of pi~_{0,3} (the profinite (2,3,infinity) triangle group, i.e. PSL_2(Z)^, containing Fhat_2 with quotient S_3), normalised by u(sigma_inf) = h sigma_inf, u(rho) = g rho, and preserving inertia classes up to a power mu.
ideas.modern_name: GT / Ihara-Drinfeld description via automorphisms of Fhat_2 ⋊ S_3, or of PSL_2(Z)^, respecting inertia
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara (1991); the S_3 / PSL_2 formulations in Lochak-Schneps and Nakamura-Schneps (late 1990s)
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche (1981) discusses pi_{0,3} with its S_3 symmetry and the 'relation de lacets'; Esquisse d'un programme mentions the Teichmüller tower in genus 0

ideas.what: Derivation of the boxed 'relation des lacets' sigma_inf(h) g = sigma_inf(f)^{-1} l_1^nu rho(f), with mu = 1 + 2 nu, linking the order-2 cocycle h and the order-3 cocycle g via f.
ideas.modern_name: Combination of Drinfeld's GT relations (I) and (II) (2-cycle and 3-cycle), with mu = 1 + 2 nu matching Drinfeld's lambda = 2m + 1
ideas.where_published: Unpublished in this form; related material in the Longue Marche

ideas.what: Transport of the loop relation from the point 0 to the points 1 and infinity via the order-3 symmetry: f_1 = rho(f) g^{-1}, f_inf = rho^2(f) rho(g)^{-1} g^{-1}.
ideas.modern_name: Cocycle bookkeeping for the S_3 action

missed.claim: These notes show Grothendieck (presumably early 1980s, before Drinfeld 1990) deriving an explicit GT-type defining relation from automorphisms of the profinite (2,3,infinity) triangle group. The derivation uses half-loops eps_i with eps_i^2 = l_i and the parametrisation mu = 1 + 2 nu. This mirrors Drinfeld's lambda = 2m + 1 convention. It is historical priority evidence rather than a new mathematical result; the content is now standard.
missed.quote: Cette relation, qui relie h et g via f, peut à juste titre s'appeler la "relation des lacets".
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents Grothendieck's independent pre-Drinfeld formulation of GT relations through PSL_2(Zhat)-type extended groups. This is relevant to the history of GT and to the 'orbifold / half-loop' presentations used by Lochak-Nakamura-Schneps.

deep.surprise_reason: The computations are a correct, routine derivation of GT-type relations that are now well known. Interest is mainly historical: an explicit pre-Drinfeld derivation in the PSL_2(Zhat) / half-loop formalism, with Drinfeld's odd-unit parametrisation mu = 1 + 2 nu. Nothing here is mathematically new to specialists.
transcription_corrections: 'on posant' should read 'en posant'; 'on explicitant' should read 'en explicitant'.
The parenthetical reads roughly '(je note donc ν ce qui était désigné par r [?] précédemment)'. The previous symbol is a different letter, not ν.
In (9), the second bracket is more plausibly '[f h σ_∞(gρ(f)^{-1})]'. The '1' after f is likely a comma or slip, not f_1.
The first line of (7) should read u(ε_1) = int(f_1^{-1})(ε_1^μ) and u(ℓ_1) = int(f_1^{-1})(ℓ_1^μ).
